Among PEFT techniques, reparameterization-based methods, particularly those that employ low-rank or sparsity structures, have attracted significant attention. However, these approaches often underperform full fine-tuning. Specifically, low-rank methods constrain the update rank, which is misaligned with the inherently high-rank nature of full fine-tuning. In contrast, sparsity-based techniques limit the flexibility of the parameter space and compromise connectivity across weights. To overcome these limitations, we explore the use of Toeplitz matrices, whose entries are constant along each diagonal, therefore providing a compact parameterization without imposing explicit rank or sparsity constraints. A straightforward approach is to update weights via a product of Toeplitz matrices. However, similar to RNNs, long multiplicative chains often lead to gradient instability. We theoretically show that products of block-wise Toeplitz matrices can approximate arbitrary matrices under shorter chain length, justifying the structural design of ToPA. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ToPA offers greater expressivity than existing low-rank and sparse parameterizations. Empirical evaluations across 21 NLP and CV datasets, spanning 5 model architectures, consistently validate the effectiveness of ToPA. Paper Title: ToPA: Block-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine-Tuning. Authors: Sicong Li, Qianqian Xu* , Zhiyong Yang , Zitai Wang , Longtao Huang, Xiaochun Cao , Qingming Huang* Abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has emerged as a prevalent strategy for adapting large pre-trained models. Among PEFT techniques, reparameterization-based methods, particularly those that employ low-rank or sparsity structures, have attracted significant attention. However, these approaches often underperform full fine-tuning. Specifically, low-rank methods constrain the update rank, which is misaligned with the inherently high-rank nature of full fine-tuning. In contrast, sparsity-based techniques limit the flexibility of the parameter space and compromise connectivity across weights. To overcome these limitations, we explore the use of Toeplitz matrices, whose entries are constant along each diagonal, therefore providing a compact parameterization without imposing explicit rank or sparsity constraints. A straightforward approach is to update weights via a product of Toeplitz matrices. However, similar to RNNs, long multiplicative chains often lead to gradient instability. To address this issue, we propose ToPA, a more refined version of this idea that replaces standard Toeplitz matrices with block-wise Toeplitz, greatly increasing each factor's capacity and shortening the chain, thereby stabilizing training and improving expressiveness. We theoretically show that products of block-wise Toeplitz matrices can approximate arbitrary matrices under shorter chain length, justifying the structural design of ToPA. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ToPA offers greater expressivity than existing low-rank and sparse parameterizations. Empirical evaluations across 21 NLP and CV datasets, spanning 5 model architectures, consistently validate the effectiveness of ToPA. Installation Use Python 3.10 or later and install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA environment, then install the dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt Datasets Download the prepared datasets from PiSSA on Hugging Face . Place the commonsense , metamath , and python directories under pissa-dataset/ in the repository root, using the following layout: pissa-dataset/ ├── commonsense/ │ ├── train.json │ └── test.json ├── metamath/ │ ├── train.json │ └── test.json └── python/ ├── train.json └── test.json Task Training data Evaluation commonsense Commonsense170K Eight commonsense benchmarks metamath MetaMathQA GSM8K and MATH python Python subset of CodeFeedback HumanEval and MBPP Scripts Training and evaluation launchers are provided in scripts/ , grouped by task and backbone. For example: # Mathematical reasoning bash scripts/metamath/train_topa.sh # Commonsense reasoning bash scripts/commonsense/train_topa.sh # Code generation bash scripts/python/train_topa.sh Using ToPA in Python ToPA is implemented in peft/tuners/topa/ . The local PEFT 0.14.0 package retains the original tuners and adds ToPAConfig and ToPAModel . from peft import TaskType , ToPAConfig , get_peft_model config = ToPAConfig ( task_type = TaskType . CAUSAL_LM , target_modules = [ "q_proj" , "v_proj" ], toep_r = 3 , block_size = 512 , ) model = get_peft_model ( base_model , config ) toep_r is the Toeplitz factor chain length. block_size is the size of each Toeplitz block and must divide the input width. For input width n , the number of blocks per dimension is n / block_size . Saved adapters use peft_type="TOPA" and the topa_ weight prefix. Adapters saved before this rename need their configuration and weight keys converted before loading with this version. Citation If ToPA is useful for your research, please cite our paper: @inproceedings { li2026topa , title = { ToPA: Block-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine-Tuning } , author = { Sicong Li and Qianqian Xu and Zhiyong Yang and Zitai Wang and Longtao Huang and Xiaochun Cao and Qingming Huang } , booktitle = { Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems } , year = { 2026 } } Acknowledgements The training and evaluation pipeline is based on PiSSA , and the adapter infrastructure is based on Hugging Face PEFT . Dataset provenance is documented on the PiSSA dataset page . selected_records.title: ToPA: Block-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine-Tuning

article.body:
Researchers propose ToPA fine-tuning method using block-wise Toeplitz matrices

Seven researchers have proposed ToPA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that uses block-wise Toeplitz matrices to adapt pre-trained models. Their paper was submitted to arXiv on Oct. 16, 2026.

The authors say existing reparameterization approaches can limit model updates: low-rank methods constrain their rank, while sparsity-based techniques restrict flexibility and connections among weights. ToPA instead uses matrices whose entries are constant along each diagonal, providing what the researchers describe as a compact parameterization without explicit rank or sparsity constraints.

The paper says a straightforward method based on multiplying standard Toeplitz matrices can create long chains that risk gradient instability. ToPA replaces those matrices with block-wise versions, which the authors say increase the capacity of each factor and shorten the chain. They argue this design improves expressiveness and stabilizes training.

The researchers also say their theoretical analysis shows that products of block-wise Toeplitz matrices can approximate arbitrary matrices with shorter chains. They report evaluations across 21 natural-language-processing and computer-vision datasets and five model architectures, describing the results as consistently validating the method’s effectiveness. The abstract does not provide individual performance figures.

The authors are Sicong Li, Qianqian Xu, Zhiyong Yang, Zitai Wang, Longtao Huang, Xiaochun Cao and Qingming Huang. A NeurIPS 2026 conference listing schedules a poster presentation of the paper for Dec. 9 in Sydney. The paper’s abstract presents the method and its evaluation; it does not establish deployment in operational systems.
